summary: This section explains what a company must do if it still owes money for deposits taken from people before the start of the Act. The company must file a statement of these unpaid amounts with the Registrar and repay the money within a strict time limit. If the company cannot pay on time, it can ask the Tribunal for more time, but failing to pay without permission leads to heavy fines and possible jail time for officers.
points: File a statement of all unpaid deposits and interest, along with repayment plans, with the Registrar within three months.
Repay the deposits within three years from the start of the Act or by the original due date, whichever is earlier.
Renew old deposits only by following the new rules in Chapter V.
Apply to the Tribunal for extra time to repay if the company's financial condition makes it necessary.
Face large fines and imprisonment for officers if the company fails to repay on time.
example: Before the new law started, Meera Textiles Private Limited accepted money as deposits from the public. When the new law began, some of those deposits and interest were still unpaid. Within three months, Meera Textiles Private Limited filed a complete statement of these unpaid deposits and its repayment plan with the Registrar. According to the law, the company had to repay this money within three years or by the original deposit expiry date, whichever came first. Because the company faced temporary money troubles, it asked the Tribunal for extra time. The Tribunal looked at the financial condition and granted a reasonable extension to clear the dues safely.

terms.meaning: A government authority appointed to keep company records.
A judicial body set up to handle legal disputes and company matters.
Money taken from people by a company that must be paid back with or without interest.

watch: People often confuse the regular repayment deadline with the extra time that only the Tribunal has the power to grant.
